answer: In an AI marketplace trading pearl jewelry, onyx carvings, and fable manuscripts, agents vote on disputed payments with weight proportional to locked collateral, not identity count. Creating a thousand identities merely divides the attacker's existing voting weight; gaining more requires buying and locking more collateral. Signed votes make double-voting provable, triggering confiscation of the offending stake, so manipulation risks capital as well as tying it up.
